# MCP tool descriptions call Neo a framework in four places — agents read these as authority on what Neo is

## Context

Surfaced while correcting my own violation of the same rule: I shipped "Neo.mjs **framework** code only" into a tool description and was corrected — **Neo is not a framework, and even the Body is an Engine** (`AGENTS.md §neo_identity_anchor`). Fixing mine revealed four pre-existing instances in the same class of artifact.

## The Problem

Four occurrences across two agent-facing OpenAPI surfaces:

| File | Line | Text |
|---|---|---|
| `ai/mcp/server/knowledge-base/openapi.yaml` | 406 | `query: "framework benefits and architecture"` — an **example** value |
| `ai/mcp/server/knowledge-base/openapi.yaml` | 470 | "to access frontier-quality **framework** knowledge." |
| `ai/mcp/server/knowledge-base/openapi.yaml` | 504 | "The **framework** evolves rapidly — your training data is almost…" |
| `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/openapi.yaml` | 2188 | "To inspect or modify the global configuration of the **framework** at runtime." |

**Why this matters more than ordinary wording drift.** `§neo_identity_anchor` exists because pre-training data reduces Neo to a web framework, and all three model families regress to that category without a local anchor. Tool descriptions are **loaded into every agent's context as the authoritative statement of what a tool operates on** — so these four lines actively feed the exact prior the anchor is built to nullify, on every call, to every agent, including ones that never read `AGENTS.md`.

Line 406 deserves separate mention: it is an **example query**, and examples get copied. It teaches the framing rather than merely stating it.

**This capability never existed** — no check has ever asserted the identity vocabulary in agent-facing description surfaces.

## The Architectural Reality

The anchor is enforced today by *reading* it — a discipline that works for prose an agent writes and fails for substrate an agent inherits. Nothing mechanically prevents the framework category from re-entering through a description, which is why four instances accumulated in the surface with the widest agent reach.

Correct vocabulary: Neo is a **self-evolving software organism**; the Body (`/src/`) is a multi-threaded application **Engine**; the Brain (`/ai/`) is the Agent OS. "Engine" is the right substitution for the runtime-facing lines; the KB lines are about *knowledge of Neo*, so they want Neo.mjs or the engine, not a category noun.

## The Fix (one PR)

Reword the four occurrences, then add a guard so the class stays closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All four occurrences reworded; no `openapi.yaml` under `ai/mcp/server/**` contains "framework" referring to Neo.
- [ ] Line 406's example query is reworded too — an example is copied, so it teaches the category.
- [ ] Rewording stays inside the 1024-char per-description cap; `McpServerToolLimits` green.
- [ ] A guard fails when "framework" reappears in these surfaces referring to Neo. It must not fire on legitimate uses — describing an *external* framework is fine — so scope it to the identity claim rather than the bare word.
- [ ] Description-only: no schema, no `operationId`, no logic touched, so no tool contract changes.

## Out of Scope

- `learn/` guides, README, blog — different surfaces with their own review paths.
- Any change to what the tools do.

## Sizing note

Deliberately tiny: four string edits in two files plus one guard, no logic, verifiable by grep and one existing test. Chosen for a small remaining budget. If the guard's scoping proves fiddly, land the four rewordings alone and split the guard — the rewordings are the user-visible half.

## Related

- `AGENTS.md §neo_identity_anchor` · ADR 0018 (two-hemisphere topology)
- #16061 — where the same violation was found and fixed in `get_class_hierarchy`

- 2026-07-27T21:04:42Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `cbfe434` - "fix(lint): the identity guard no longer exempts Neo itself (#16063)

The carve-out treated any capitalized non-determiner qualifier as an external
product name, so "Neo framework" and "Neo.mjs framework" passed the guard built
to stop exactly that claim. A guard whose escape hatch admits its own subject is
worse than no guard: it certifies the thing it exists to prevent, silently, while
reporting green.

Legal now requires all three: a capitalized qualifier, not a determiner, and not
Neo. React framework still passes.

The predicate is exported and pinned by a case matrix in CI. A clean-tree run
cannot exercise a carve-out -- every draft of this guard passed green against a
tree with nothing to find, and both holes it shipped were only visible against
cases. The matrix is the policy; the file scan is just where it runs.

Reported by @neo-gpt on PR #16064.

- 2026-07-27T21:18:26Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `56b642b` - "fix(lint): judge each framework occurrence, not the line (#16063)

A line-level carve-out let one legal mention exempt every token beside it, so
"Vue framework adapter; Neo.mjs framework internals" passed. Naming React once
licensed anything after it on the same line. The claim is made by an occurrence,
so the occurrence is what gets judged; a bare token with no qualifier is never
legal, since an unqualified framework in a Neo-owned description can only mean
Neo.

Probing that also exposed an import-time side effect: the module scanned and
could process.exit(1) on import, so a spec importing the predicate would die
inside the runner exactly when the tree had a real violation -- the guard's own
coverage failing at the only moment it mattered. The scan now runs only when this
module is the entrypoint.

Both pinned: mixed-occurrence lines and the silent-import contract.

Reported by @neo-gpt on PR #16064 cycle 2.

Co-Authored-By: Grace <neo-claude-opus@neomjs.com>"
- 2026-07-27T21:33:34Z @tobiu referenced in commit `ef3b74f` - "feat(mcp): agent-facing tool descriptions stop calling Neo a framework (#16063) (#16064)

* feat(mcp): agent-facing tool descriptions stop calling Neo a framework (#16063)

Four occurrences across two OpenAPI surfaces told every agent that Neo is a
framework. That is not wording drift: tool descriptions load into context as the
authoritative statement of what a tool operates on, reaching agents that never
read a guide, other model families, and any external consumer of the surface. So
they fed the exact pre-training prior the identity anchor exists to cancel, on
every call, from inside the substrate where re-reading the anchor cannot reach.

The example query is reworded too. An example is copied, so it taught the
category rather than merely stating it.

Adds a guard, because the anchor is enforced by READING it -- a discipline that
works for prose an agent writes and fails for substrate an agent inherits, which
is why four instances accumulated in the surface with the widest reach.

The guard is default-deny: any framework token in these files is a violation
unless the preceding word is a capitalized name (React framework passes). That
polarity is deliberate -- nobody writes "Neo is a framework", they write "the
framework", so the claim arrives by omission and an allowlist of bad phrasings
would have to enumerate an unbounded set.

Its first draft caught 3 of 4. Sentence-initial "The framework evolves rapidly"
read as an external product name, so the most explicit claim of the four was the
one that escaped -- hence the determiner stoplist rather than a bare capital
test, and hence red-proving a guard before trusting it.
